## Code

```{r data setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmnet)
library(pls)
library(boot)
library(gridExtra)

# no setwd() needed: knitr runs the chunks in the folder of this .Rmd, so keep the
# .Rmd and the csv files in the same folder (setwd() in a chunk is reset after that chunk)
athletics  <- read.csv("data_783996yw.csv")
prediction <- read.csv("predictions-2.csv")
```

```{r data cleanup, include=FALSE}

# 1. Inspect data

dim(athletics) #check size, variables and distribution of revenue, the variable of interest
str(athletics)
summary(athletics$revenue)

na_counts <- colSums(is.na(athletics)) #check missing values for each variable/column
na_counts[na_counts > 0] #show only cols with missing values. hc na counts match with hc salary na counts

table(no_men_teams = athletics$teams_men == 0, hc_men_missing = is.na(athletics$hc_men)) #institution with no men's team can't have men's hc!
table(no_women_teams = athletics$teams_women == 0, hc_women_missing = is.na(athletics$hc_women)) #same for women
min(athletics$ac_men, na.rm = TRUE) #ac counts are never 0 (min = 1), so na in ac_men means no acs at the institution

sum(!is.na(athletics$ac_men)   & is.na(athletics$ac_salary_men)) #how many institutions HAVE acs but no salary reported?
sum(!is.na(athletics$ac_women) & is.na(athletics$ac_salary_women)) #probably volunteers (eada leaves them out of the average salary)

table(athletics$classification) #get an overview of categorical variables and their levels
table(athletics$sector) #some classifications and sectors have very small levels:
                        #NCCAA Division I, Private for-profit 4-year or above, Private nonprofit 2-year

revenue <- ggplot(athletics, aes(revenue / 1e6)) +  #inspect the revenue variable itself, divide revenue by one million before plotting for easier reading
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "blue", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Revenue of athletics programs", x = "Revenue (in million USD)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
revenue #a very skewed histogram...log it to combat skewness

logrevenue <- ggplot(athletics, aes(log(revenue))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "purple", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Log revenue", x = "log(revenue)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
logrevenue

grid.arrange(revenue, logrevenue, ncol = 2) #both histograms next to each other (for the report)

classifications <- ggplot(athletics, aes(x = reorder(classification, revenue, median), y = log(revenue))) + #how strongly does revenue depend on the division?
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") + coord_flip() +                                                         #check with boxplots of log revenue per
  labs(title = "Log revenue by classification", x = NULL, y = "log(revenue)") +                             #classification, sorted by median
  theme_minimal()
classifications

# 2. Clean up the data

count_vars  <- c("ugrad_men", "ugrad_women", "athletes_men", "athletes_women", "teams_men", "teams_women", # the predictors are grouped by variable type
                 grep("^partic_", names(athletics), value = TRUE), #add all the partic_ variables more quickly
                 "hc_men", "hc_women", "ac_men", "ac_women") #logged
salary_vars <- c("hc_salary_men", "hc_salary_women", "ac_salary_men", "ac_salary_women") #logged
share_vars  <- c("hc_fulltime_share", "hc_female_share") # 0 to 1, not logged
num_vars    <- c(count_vars, salary_vars, share_vars)   # all 28 numerical predictors

fixed_coaches <- function(x) {
  for (s in c("men", "women")) { #loop runs once for men's and women's variables (hc, ac, salaries)
    hc <- paste0("hc_", s); ac <- paste0("ac_", s) #becomes hc_men and ac_men, then hc_women and ac_women
    hs <- paste0("hc_salary_", s); as <- paste0("ac_salary_", s) #same for the salary columns
    no_hc <- is.na(x[[hc]])          # institutions without hcs
    no_ac <- is.na(x[[ac]])          # institutions without acs
    x[[hc]][no_hc] <- 0              # missing coaches become 0 (e.g. no men's team -> no men's hc)
    x[[ac]][no_ac] <- 0
    x[[hs]][no_hc & is.na(x[[hs]])] <- 0 # no coaches -> salary also becomes 0 (nothing is paid)
    x[[as]][no_ac & is.na(x[[as]])] <- 0 # coaches present but no salary (volunteers?) stay na -> imputed later
  }
  x
}

logged_vars <- function(x) { #skewed variables, we log them
  for (v in c(count_vars, salary_vars)) x[[v]] <- log1p(x[[v]]) #log(x + 1) in case x is 0
  x
}

athletics_new  <- athletics %>% fixed_coaches() #the function fixed_coaches is applied to both datasets
prediction_new <- prediction %>% fixed_coaches()

colSums(is.na(athletics_new[num_vars]))[colSums(is.na(athletics_new[num_vars])) > 0] #only some ac salaries are still missing (the potential volunteers)

athletics_new$log_revenue <- log(athletics_new$revenue) #this is the target variable

athletics_new$classification  <- factor(athletics_new$classification) #categorical variables transformed to factors, for both datasets
athletics_new$sector          <- factor(athletics_new$sector)
prediction_new$classification <- factor(prediction_new$classification, levels = levels(athletics_new$classification)) #same levels -> same dummies
prediction_new$sector         <- factor(prediction_new$sector, levels = levels(athletics_new$sector))
stopifnot(!anyNA(prediction_new$classification), !anyNA(prediction_new$sector)) #check: every level in prediction exists in the data

skewness_fun <- function(x) { #skewness: 0 = symmetric, > 0 = long right tail
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  mean((x - mean(x))^3) / sd(x)^3
}
skew_tab <- data.frame( #skewness before and after logging, to motivate the log
  Variable = c("revenue", count_vars, salary_vars),
  Raw = sapply(c("revenue", count_vars, salary_vars), function(v) skewness_fun(athletics_new[[v]])),
  Log = c(skewness_fun(athletics_new$log_revenue),
          sapply(c(count_vars, salary_vars), function(v) skewness_fun(log1p(athletics_new[[v]])))))
print(skew_tab, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)

athletics_new  <- logged_vars(athletics_new) #log the skewed predictors in both datasets
prediction_new <- logged_vars(prediction_new)
```

```{r split, include=FALSE}

# 3. Train/test split and imputation (on train only)

set.seed(123) #reproducible random 80/20 split
train_index <- sample(seq_len(nrow(athletics_new)), size = floor(0.8 * nrow(athletics_new)))
train_data  <- athletics_new[train_index, ]
test_data   <- athletics_new[-train_index, ]
table(train_data$classification) #are all levels in the training set?

train_medians <- sapply(train_data[num_vars], median, na.rm = TRUE) #medians from the training data only (no leakage)
impute <- function(x) { #remaining na (salaries of potential volunteers) -> training median
  for (v in num_vars) x[[v]][is.na(x[[v]])] <- train_medians[v]
  x
}
train_data     <- impute(train_data)
test_data      <- impute(test_data)
prediction_new <- impute(prediction_new)
stopifnot(!anyNA(train_data[num_vars]), !anyNA(test_data[num_vars]), !anyNA(prediction_new[num_vars])) #check: no na left

cor_tab <- sort(sapply(train_data[num_vars], cor, y = train_data$log_revenue), decreasing = TRUE) #correlation with log revenue
round(cor_tab, 2) #salaries and coaches correlate strongly: in eada revenue must cover expenses
```

```{r pca, include=FALSE}

# 4. PCA on the 28 numerical predictors (training data, standardised)

X_train <- train_data[, num_vars]
X_test  <- test_data[, num_vars]
p       <- ncol(X_train)

pca_model   <- prcomp(X_train, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE) #scale = pca on the correlation matrix (different units)
eigenvalues <- pca_model$sdev^2              #variance of each component
vaf         <- eigenvalues / sum(eigenvalues) #variance accounted for
cum_vaf     <- cumsum(vaf)                    #cumulative vaf
pca_summary <- data.frame(PC = seq_along(eigenvalues), Eigenvalue = eigenvalues, VAF = vaf, CumulativeVAF = cum_vaf)
round(pca_summary, 3)

# 4a. four simple criteria
k_kaiser   <- sum(eigenvalues > 1)      #kaiser: eigenvalue > 1
k_jolliffe <- sum(eigenvalues > 0.7)    #jolliffe: eigenvalue > 0.7
k_vaf80    <- which(cum_vaf >= 0.80)[1] #first pc where 80% is reached

scree <- ggplot(pca_summary, aes(PC, Eigenvalue)) + #scree plot: look for the elbow
  geom_line(color = "steelblue") + geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_len(p)) +
  labs(title = "Scree plot", x = "Principal component", y = "Eigenvalue") +
  theme_minimal()
scree

# 4b. permutation test: shuffle each column separately -> no correlation left, pcs only reflect chance
set.seed(123)
perm_vaf <- t(replicate(1000, {
  X_perm <- apply(X_train, 2, sample)
  ev <- prcomp(X_perm, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)$sdev^2
  ev / sum(ev)
}))
perm_q95 <- apply(perm_vaf, 2, quantile, probs = 0.95)                #95% chance level per pc
perm_p   <- sapply(seq_len(p), function(j) mean(perm_vaf[, j] >= vaf[j])) #p-value per pc
perm_tab <- data.frame(PC = seq_len(p), VAF = vaf, Perm95 = perm_q95, p_value = perm_p)
round(perm_tab, 3)
k_perm <- which(vaf <= perm_q95)[1] - 1 #keep pcs up to the first non-significant one

permutation <- ggplot(perm_tab, aes(PC)) + #blue above red = keep
  geom_line(aes(y = VAF, color = "Observed")) + geom_point(aes(y = VAF, color = "Observed")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Perm95, color = "Permutation 95%")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Observed" = "steelblue", "Permutation 95%" = "red")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_len(p)) +
  labs(title = "Permutation test for the number of PCs", x = "Principal component",
       y = "Variance accounted for", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
permutation

# 4c. bootstrap of kaiser's rule and of vaf
my_boot_pca <- function(x, ind) { #pca on the resampled rows, return the eigenvalues
  prcomp(x[ind, ], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)$sdev^2
}
set.seed(123)
fit_boot  <- boot(data = X_train, statistic = my_boot_pca, R = 1000)
eigs_boot <- fit_boot$t #1000 x p matrix of bootstrapped eigenvalues

kaiser_boot <- data.frame(PC = seq_len(p), Eigenvalue = eigenvalues, #95% ci per eigenvalue
                          Lower = apply(eigs_boot, 2, quantile, 0.025),
                          Upper = apply(eigs_boot, 2, quantile, 0.975))
kaiser_boot$Significant <- kaiser_boot$Lower > 1 #significant if the whole ci is above 1
head(kaiser_boot, 8)
k_kaiser_boot <- which(!kaiser_boot$Significant)[1] - 1

kaiserboot <- ggplot(head(kaiser_boot, 10), aes(PC, Eigenvalue)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Lower, ymax = Upper), width = 0.2) + geom_point(color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(title = "Bootstrap 95% CIs of the eigenvalues (Kaiser's rule)", x = "Principal component", y = "Eigenvalue") +
  theme_minimal()
kaiserboot

n_pc <- k_perm #chosen number of pcs (permutation test), change and motivate if you choose differently

vaf_boot <- rowSums(eigs_boot[, 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE]) / p #bootstrapped vaf of the chosen pcs
vaf_ci   <- quantile(vaf_boot, c(0.025, 0.975))
round(100 * c(VAF = cum_vaf[n_pc], vaf_ci), 1)

vaf_each_boot <- eigs_boot / p #bootstrap ci for the vaf of each chosen pc
vaf_each_ci <- data.frame(PC = 1:n_pc, VAF = vaf[1:n_pc],
                          Lower = apply(vaf_each_boot[, 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE], 2, quantile, 0.025),
                          Upper = apply(vaf_each_boot[, 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE], 2, quantile, 0.975))
round(vaf_each_ci, 3)

pc_selection <- data.frame( #overview of all methods for the report
  Method = c("Kaiser (eigenvalue > 1)", "Jolliffe (eigenvalue > 0.7)", "80% cumulative VAF",
             "Permutation test", "Bootstrapped Kaiser"),
  PCs = c(k_kaiser, k_jolliffe, k_vaf80, k_perm, k_kaiser_boot))
pc_selection

# 4d. interpretation
loadings <- pca_model$rotation[, 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE] #weights of the variables in each pc
round(loadings, 2)
var_pc_cor  <- sweep(loadings, 2, pca_model$sdev[1:n_pc], "*") #correlation variable-pc = loading * sd of pc
communality <- rowSums(var_pc_cor^2) #share of each variable explained by the chosen pcs
round(cbind(var_pc_cor, Communality = communality), 2)

score_plot   <- data.frame(PC1 = pca_model$x[, 1], PC2 = pca_model$x[, 2], Division = train_data$classification)
loading_plot <- data.frame(Variable = rownames(pca_model$rotation),
                           PC1 = pca_model$rotation[, 1], PC2 = pca_model$rotation[, 2])
arrow_scale <- 0.8 * min(max(abs(score_plot$PC1)) / max(abs(loading_plot$PC1)), #stretch arrows to the scale of the scores
                         max(abs(score_plot$PC2)) / max(abs(loading_plot$PC2)))
biplot_pca <- ggplot(score_plot, aes(PC1, PC2)) + #points = institutions, arrows = variables
  geom_point(aes(color = Division), alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  geom_segment(data = loading_plot, aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = PC1 * arrow_scale, yend = PC2 * arrow_scale),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "black", arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.15, "cm"))) +
  geom_text(data = loading_plot, aes(x = PC1 * arrow_scale, y = PC2 * arrow_scale, label = Variable),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.6, check_overlap = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "PCA biplot", x = paste0("PC1 (", round(100 * vaf[1], 1), "%)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", round(100 * vaf[2], 1), "%)")) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.text = element_text(size = 6))
biplot_pca
```

```{r pcr, include=FALSE}

# 5. Principal component regression

pcr_data <- train_data[, c("log_revenue", num_vars)] #variant a: pcr on the numerical predictors
set.seed(123)
fit_pcr <- pcr(log_revenue ~ ., data = pcr_data, scale = TRUE, validation = "CV", segments = 10) #10-fold cv for every number of pcs
summary(fit_pcr)

cv_rmsep <- RMSEP(fit_pcr, estimate = "CV")$val[1, 1, -1] #cv error per number of pcs (without intercept-only model)
k_cv     <- which.min(cv_rmsep)                           #number of pcs with the lowest cv error
k_cv_1se <- selectNcomp(fit_pcr, method = "onesigma")     #smallest number within one se
c(k_cv = k_cv, k_cv_1se = k_cv_1se)

validationplot(fit_pcr, val.type = "RMSEP", main = "PCR: cross-validated RMSEP (log revenue)")
abline(v = n_pc, lty = 2, col = "red") #red line = chosen n_pc

train_scores <- data.frame(pca_model$x[, 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE], #variant b: pc scores + dummies
                           classification = train_data$classification,
                           sector = train_data$sector,
                           log_revenue = train_data$log_revenue)
test_scores  <- data.frame(predict(pca_model, newdata = X_test)[, 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE], #test projected on the training pca
                           classification = test_data$classification,
                           sector = test_data$sector)
fit_pcr_dum <- lm(log_revenue ~ ., data = train_scores)
summary(fit_pcr_dum)
```

```{r ridge, include=FALSE}

# 6. Ridge regression

form_x  <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(c(num_vars, "classification", "sector"), collapse = " + ")))
x_train <- model.matrix(form_x, data = train_data)[, -1] #matrix with dummies, [, -1] drops the intercept column
x_test  <- model.matrix(form_x, data = test_data)[, -1]
y_train <- train_data$log_revenue
y_test  <- test_data$log_revenue

set.seed(123)
cv_ridge <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 0, nfolds = 10) #alpha = 0 -> ridge, 10-fold cv over a grid of lambdas
c(lambda_min = cv_ridge$lambda.min, lambda_1se = cv_ridge$lambda.1se)

plot(cv_ridge) #cv error against log(lambda)
plot(cv_ridge$glmnet.fit, xvar = "lambda") #coefficient paths: shrink to 0, never exactly 0
abline(v = log(c(cv_ridge$lambda.min, cv_ridge$lambda.1se)), lty = 2)

ridge_coef <- data.frame(Variable   = rownames(coef(cv_ridge, s = "lambda.min")), #coefficients on log scale
                         lambda_min = as.numeric(coef(cv_ridge, s = "lambda.min")),
                         lambda_1se = as.numeric(coef(cv_ridge, s = "lambda.1se")))
ridge_coef
```

```{r evaluation, include=FALSE}

# 7. Evaluation on log scale and on revenue scale

rmse  <- function(y, yhat) sqrt(mean((y - yhat)^2))
mae   <- function(y, yhat) mean(abs(y - yhat))
mdape <- function(y, yhat) median(abs(y - yhat) / y) #median absolute percentage error

pred_log <- list( #test predictions of log revenue
  "PCR (numerical, n_pc)"     = as.numeric(predict(fit_pcr, newdata = test_data, ncomp = n_pc)),
  "PCR (numerical, CV ncomp)" = as.numeric(predict(fit_pcr, newdata = test_data, ncomp = k_cv)),
  "PCR + dummies"             = as.numeric(predict(fit_pcr_dum, newdata = test_scores)),
  "Ridge lambda.min"          = as.numeric(predict(cv_ridge, newx = x_test, s = "lambda.min")),
  "Ridge lambda.1se"          = as.numeric(predict(cv_ridge, newx = x_test, s = "lambda.1se")))
fit_log <- list( #fitted values on the training set, for the smearing factor
  "PCR (numerical, n_pc)"     = as.numeric(predict(fit_pcr, ncomp = n_pc)),
  "PCR (numerical, CV ncomp)" = as.numeric(predict(fit_pcr, ncomp = k_cv)),
  "PCR + dummies"             = as.numeric(fitted(fit_pcr_dum)),
  "Ridge lambda.min"          = as.numeric(predict(cv_ridge, newx = x_train, s = "lambda.min")),
  "Ridge lambda.1se"          = as.numeric(predict(cv_ridge, newx = x_train, s = "lambda.1se")))
smear <- sapply(fit_log, function(f) mean(exp(y_train - f))) #duan's smearing factor: exp(pred) * smear = mean revenue

rev_test <- test_data$revenue
eval_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pred_log), function(m) { #one row per model
  pl <- pred_log[[m]]
  data.frame(Model = m,
             RMSE_log = rmse(y_test, pl),
             MAE_log  = mae(y_test, pl),
             R2_log   = 1 - sum((y_test - pl)^2) / sum((y_test - mean(y_test))^2),
             RMSE_rev_naive_M = rmse(rev_test, exp(pl)) / 1e6,
             RMSE_rev_smear_M = rmse(rev_test, exp(pl) * smear[m]) / 1e6,
             MAE_rev_naive_M  = mae(rev_test, exp(pl)) / 1e6,
             MdAPE_naive      = mdape(rev_test, exp(pl)),
             Smearing         = smear[m])
}))
eval_tab <- rbind(eval_tab, data.frame( #benchmark: everyone gets the training mean
  Model = "Null (mean log revenue)",
  RMSE_log = rmse(y_test, mean(y_train)), MAE_log = mae(y_test, mean(y_train)), R2_log = 0,
  RMSE_rev_naive_M = rmse(rev_test, exp(mean(y_train))) / 1e6,
  RMSE_rev_smear_M = rmse(rev_test, mean(train_data$revenue)) / 1e6,
  MAE_rev_naive_M  = mae(rev_test, exp(mean(y_train))) / 1e6,
  MdAPE_naive      = mdape(rev_test, exp(mean(y_train))),
  Smearing = NA))
print(eval_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)

err_by_class <- data.frame(classification = test_data$classification, #where do the dollar errors come from?
                           abs_err_log = abs(y_test - pred_log[["Ridge lambda.min"]]),
                           abs_err_rev = abs(rev_test - exp(pred_log[["Ridge lambda.min"]]))) %>%
  group_by(classification) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), MAE_log = mean(abs_err_log), MAE_rev_M = mean(abs_err_rev) / 1e6,
            share_of_total_abs_err = sum(abs_err_rev)) %>%
  mutate(share_of_total_abs_err = share_of_total_abs_err / sum(share_of_total_abs_err)) %>%
  arrange(desc(MAE_rev_M))
print(err_by_class, n = Inf) #fbs schools cause most of the dollar error

obs_pred <- data.frame(Observed = y_test, PCR = pred_log[["PCR + dummies"]], Ridge = pred_log[["Ridge lambda.min"]]) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Observed, names_to = "Model", values_to = "Predicted")
observed_predicted <- ggplot(obs_pred, aes(Predicted, Observed)) + #points on the red line = perfect prediction
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) + geom_abline(color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ Model) +
  labs(title = "Test set: observed vs predicted log revenue") + theme_minimal()
observed_predicted
```

```{r predictions, include=FALSE}

# 8. Predictions for the 10 institutions

full_data <- impute(athletics_new) #all 1000 institutions, na imputed

pca_full    <- prcomp(full_data[, num_vars], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE) #pcr + dummies refitted on all data
full_scores <- data.frame(pca_full$x[, 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE],
                          classification = full_data$classification,
                          sector = full_data$sector,
                          log_revenue = full_data$log_revenue)
new_scores  <- data.frame(predict(pca_full, newdata = prediction_new[, num_vars])[, 1:n_pc, drop = FALSE],
                          classification = prediction_new$classification, sector = prediction_new$sector)
fit_pcr_full <- lm(log_revenue ~ ., data = full_scores)

x_full <- model.matrix(form_x, data = full_data)[, -1] #ridge refitted on all data with lambda.min from the training cv
x_new  <- model.matrix(form_x, data = prediction_new)[, -1]
ridge_full <- glmnet(x_full, full_data$log_revenue, alpha = 0, lambda = cv_ridge$lambda.min)

pl_pcr      <- as.numeric(predict(fit_pcr_full, newdata = new_scores)) #log revenue predictions
pl_ridge    <- as.numeric(predict(ridge_full, newx = x_new))
smear_pcr   <- mean(exp(residuals(fit_pcr_full)))
smear_ridge <- mean(exp(full_data$log_revenue - as.numeric(predict(ridge_full, newx = x_full))))

pred_out <- data.frame(id = prediction_new$id, classification = prediction_new$classification, #in million usd
                       log_rev_PCR = pl_pcr, log_rev_Ridge = pl_ridge,
                       rev_PCR_median_M   = exp(pl_pcr) / 1e6,               #median-type: exp(pred)
                       rev_PCR_mean_M     = exp(pl_pcr) * smear_pcr / 1e6,   #mean-type: exp(pred) * smearing
                       rev_Ridge_median_M = exp(pl_ridge) / 1e6,
                       rev_Ridge_mean_M   = exp(pl_ridge) * smear_ridge / 1e6)
print(pred_out, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(pred_out, "predictions_output.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
